name: Adaptive Bitrate
description: Real adaptive bitrate for Jellyfin's HLS streams. Jellyfin measures the network once, when playback starts, and offers a single quality: when the connection weakens, playback stops to buffer or restarts at a lower quality. This plugin puts a real quality ladder in every HLS stream, each step produced by Jellyfin itself with the same audio track and subtitles, so the player (web, Android, iOS) switches quality on its own, loading the new one before switching, without a cut. Lower qualities cost nothing until a player uses them. Source, documentation and issues: https://github.com/crocodile13/jellyfin-plugin-adaptive-bitrate
overview: Quality that follows the network, without a cut.

versions.changelog: 1.0.0 (Jellyfin 12.2 to 12.4): first version. Every HLS stream Jellyfin serves gets a real quality ladder: by default 4 lower qualities down to 700 kb/s, each produced by Jellyfin itself with the same audio track, subtitles (burned-in ones too) and playback session. The player (web, Android, Apple devices) steps down when the network weakens and back up when it recovers, loading the new quality before switching: no cut, no restart. A lower quality costs nothing until a player uses it. Measured on a real Jellyfin in Chrome with the network throttled to 1.6 Mb/s for a minute: 7 s of stalls instead of 46 s, on Jellyfin 12.2 and 12.4. Optional: remote players can get the adaptive stream instead of direct play (experimental). Settings page in English, French, German and Spanish.
